reason: The simulation runs end-to-end with acceptable performance, but several spec-critical metrics and behaviors are still missing (time_to_threshold, policy_effectiveness, attitude_shift, misinformation_exposure, penalties_issued) and policy-driven resource allocation is not implemented. Fixing these will significantly improve traceability to the spec and policy interpretability. With only two iterations left, one more iteration should focus on implementing these targeted changes and minor logic fixes (risk perception signal, first_adopt_day).

specific_areas: Add missing spec metrics: time_to_threshold, policy_effectiveness (inline counterfactual), attitude_shift (vs baseline), misinformation_exposure (share), penalties_issued and fines_collected
Implement PolicyAuthority.allocate_masks and call it before retailer restocking (needs-based allocation from SupplyChain)
Fix risk perception to use epidemic.public_risk_signal as prevalence input; keep adoption prevalence as social/normative influence only

Map spec parameter aliases to internal weights: peer_influence_weight -> weight_peer, policy_effect_weight -> weight_policy, information_effect_weight -> weight_media, risk_perception_weight -> weight_prevalence
Restore first_adopt_day updates when an agent wears for the first time; keep daily_new_adopters consistent
Record daily misinfo share from info broadcasts and surface in series
Expose daily penalties_issued and fines_collected series; ensure incidents match penalties
Remove unused imports and minor hygiene fixes

task_understanding.adjustments: Prioritize spec alignment over new features. Treat missing metrics and resource allocation as mandatory for the next iteration.

data_analysis.adjustments: Compute derived metrics directly from daily signals: misinfo share = anti/(pro+anti), attitude_shift vs. baseline benefit, time_to_threshold detection once, and estimated policy_effectiveness via removal of policy term from utility.

model_planning.adjustments: Insert a policy-driven allocation step before retailer restocking using unmet demand proportional distribution; plan risk signal separation (epidemic risk vs. norms) and baseline attitude capture at initialize().

code_generation.adjustments: Implement the new series and their daily updates, the allocate_masks method, alias parameter mapping, prevalence signal fix, and first_adopt_day updates. Keep changes localized and covered by simple guards.

code_verification.adjustments: Add checks that new series keys exist and are populated; assert penalties_issued equals incidents; verify time_to_threshold is set once crossing occurs; confirm policy_effectiveness is within [-1,1]; ensure removal of unused import.

simulation_execution.adjustments: Run a short smoke test (e.g., 60 days, N≈500) with and without mandates to ensure metrics populate and allocation doesn’t break restocking; validate no performance regression.

result_evaluation.adjustments: Update evaluation to report the new metrics; sanity-check that policy_effectiveness > 0 under mandates; misinfo share within [0,1]; time_to_threshold reasonable when threshold lowered (e.g., 0.5 for tests).

feedback_generation.adjustments: Provide concise, metric-focused feedback highlighting the newly added outputs and any remaining gaps, with pointers to series names and expected ranges.
